newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise, Suez to form utility powerhouse.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise, Suez to form utility powerhouse.

text.p: France's Lyonnaise des Eaux said Friday the diversified utility would take over holding company Cie de Suez to create a world heavyweight in utilities and services.
The companies were to announce details later on the deal, which ends the independence of Suez, set up in the 19th century to build the Suez Canal, a glory of French engineering.
Lyonnaise Chairman Jerome Monod told Europe 1 radio that his company would absorb Suez, a financial services and utilities company, through a friendly "merger-takeover."
The combined giant will focus on four core businesses -- energy, water distribution, waste management and communications.
Lyonnaise's "mission is to conquer the world," said Monod.
The combined group is to be called Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux.

Monod said the aim was to create a company that would boast annual turnover of 200 billion francs ($35 billion) and a stock market capitalisation of $75 billion francs ($13 billion). It would have resources to invest around 17 billion francs ($3 billion) from its first year of operation.
The boards of the two companies were meeting on Friday to approve terms of the merger, which has already won the nod from the Lyonnaise board.
Lyonnaise, which has water distribution, construction and communications businesses, has been pushing the deal as an operation that will give it extra muscle to expand abroad.

By focusing on the four core activities, analysts say Lyonnaise's construction activities and most of the financial and industrial holdings controlled by Suez -- apart from Belgian energy and services giant Tractebel -- could be up for sale.

Lyonnaise is twice the size of Suez in terms of shareholders funds and one-third bigger in share capitalisation. Suez, once one of France's grandest corporate institutions, fell victim in the early 1990s to a property slump.
